oneLiner: Closed at 7,623.68 Friday, down 0.52% on the day and 0.47% on the week, about 2.5% below the record close of 7,818.93 set on October 6.
intro: The S&P 500 closed at 7,623.68 on Friday, October 23, down 0.52% on the day and about 0.47% on the week, its second weekly loss in a row. That leaves the index roughly 2.5% below its record close of 7,818.93 from October 6. A Thursday slide in AI-linked technology shares and higher oil prices on Middle East tensions were the main themes of the week.

performance.heading: How the index has done
performance.body: The strip above shows SPY ending a choppy week little changed to lower. The index itself slipped about 0.47% over the five sessions: it rose on Tuesday and Wednesday, then fell about 1.2% on Thursday as AI-linked technology shares dropped, and lost another 0.52% on Friday. The cards above track SPY, so readings there may differ slightly from the index figures here.

chart.body: The chart above plots SPY against its own moving-average lines over the same stretch. The index climbed for two sessions early in the week, then gave back ground on Thursday and Friday, a pattern that may matter to chart watchers. Exact positions on SPY may differ a little from the index figures quoted here.

levels.body: The October 6 record close of 7,818.93 is the nearest marker above, and Friday's close sits about 2.5% below it. The week's highest close came midweek, near 7,757 on Wednesday, October 21. The Price zones and Key levels cards above show where those levels sit on SPY today.

signals.heading: Momentum in plain words
signals.body: Momentum looked mixed this week: two gains early on, then a sharp Thursday drop led by chip stocks, when the Nasdaq Composite had its worst day since June. Friday's decline was shallower and some chip stocks rebounded. The panel above shows today's RSI and MACD readings on SPY, which may help show how much momentum has faded.

change.heading: The weekly and monthly pattern
change.body: Close to close, the index fell about 0.47% this week, after a bigger loss last week, and sits roughly 2.5% under its record. It rose about 0.3% on Tuesday and about 0.6% on Wednesday, then dropped about 1.2% on Thursday and 0.52% on Friday as technology shares wobbled.

marketRead: The S&P 500 ended the week at 7,623.68, down about 0.47% and roughly 2.5% below its October 6 record close of 7,818.93. It was a two-way week. The index rose about 0.3% on Tuesday, October 20, as oil retreated on hopes for Middle East diplomacy and Treasury yields eased after weak housing data, then added about 0.6% on Wednesday as technology rebounded. Thursday, October 22 reversed that: the index fell about 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite had its worst day since June as worries about AI spending and debt hit chip stocks, with Meta down about 7% after its results.

Oil and rates framed the backdrop. Brent crude reached its highest level since late April after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, with Iran-related risk also in focus, and the energy sector hit a record high on Friday, according to Reuters. The 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.1% early in the week and closed under 5% on Thursday and was back near 5% on Friday. CME FedWatch put the chance of an October rate rise at about 7% after Thursday's close, ahead of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, where Reuters said a hold is expected, with attention turning to December.

Breadth was middling: about 56% of S&P 500 members were above their 200-day average and 58% above their 50-day average at Friday's close, according to ChartRow. The optimistic case is that yields have eased back under 5%, the chance of an October rate rise looks small and roughly a third of the index's companies report next week, giving AI spending a chance to prove itself. The cautious case is that oil is climbing, University of Michigan consumer sentiment sits near a record low and investors have turned wary of AI debt and spending, a theme that has hit the index twice in two weeks. Next week may hinge on the Fed's Wednesday decision and results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon.

points.label: Catalyst
points.text: AI-spending worries hit chip stocks and Meta on Thursday, while oil climbed on Middle East tensions.

points.label: Breadth
points.text: About 56% of S&P 500 members were above their 200-day average at Friday's close, and 58% above their 50-day average.

points.label: Rates
points.text: The 10-year yield closed under 5% on Thursday; CME FedWatch put October rate-rise odds near 7% that day.

watchDown: The index slips further from the October 6 record close of 7,818.93 as AI-spending worries linger.
Oil keeps climbing on Middle East tensions, keeping inflation worries and Treasury yields elevated.
Big technology earnings next week disappoint, adding to questions around AI spending and debt.
The Fed's October 27-28 meeting brings a more cautious tone on inflation than investors expect.
watchUp: The index recovers this week's losses and heads back toward the October 6 record close of 7,818.93.
The 10-year Treasury yield stays under 5% as October rate-rise bets remain faint.
Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon results show AI spending paying off, easing this week's worries.
Breadth improves beyond today's readings of about 56% and 58% as more stocks join in.
